thread:
maria-support: Hey team — customer ACCT-998 reported that their monthly credits hit 0 two hours before their expected refill. They say their app hit the usual nightly batch and everything dropped off at ~22:05 local (customer timezone CET). Can we confirm where resets happen and any DST edge cases?

jordan-cs: Do we know whether they're on a legacy billing timezone setting or standard UTC-based cycles? Last time we had a weird early reset it was because the customer DNS/edge reported logs in local time and they misread it.

maria-support: I asked for their billing-cycle start date and account settings. They replied: "billing_start: 2024-07-15 00:00 Europe/Berlin" and attached a screenshot showing depletion at 22:05 CET on 2026-03-28. They said our dashboard shows 'next refill: 2026-03-29 00:00' but credits already zeroed at 22:05.

tim-billing: By default hosted monthly credits refill at 00:00 UTC. We do not refill per-customer timezone unless they have a legacy tenant flag; I can check for that flag on the account.

ryan-ops: Quick check — daylight savings (CET->CEST) switched on 2026-03-29 01:00 local I think. If the customer's local clock jumped, could logs and the dashboard be displaying local times that make it look early while the refill still occurred at 00:00 UTC?

maria-support: The customer insists tokens were exhausted before midnight UTC. They provided these response headers from a failed request around the time: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-credits-remaining: 0
x-credits-reset: 1776405600
x-rate-limit-reset: 1776405600
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2026 21:05:07 GMT
```

maria-support: Header x-credits-reset in epoch 1776405600 converts to Sun, 28 Mar 2026 21:00:00 GMT — that looks off if refill is at 00:00 UTC.

tim-billing: That header is the next scheduled reset for the current quota window, computed when the quota bucket was created. If the account had a manual proration or a plan change that shortened the current window, the x-credits-reset could be earlier. I’ll inspect billing events for ACCT-998.

jordan-cs: Customer batch job is big — ~1.2M tokens nightly. Any chance their burst buffer plus cached prefix usage dropped them unexpectedly? Also confirm whether they were on Dedicated vs Hosted? Burst semantics differ.

maria-support: They are on hosted API, single workspace. They said "no recent plan change". I requested a full token usage CSV from their dashboard — they sent back a CSV with many small jobs plus one big job at 20:58 UTC.

ryan-ops: I pulled usage from our ingestion logs for ACCT-998 around that day. Here's a sanitized snippet: 

```
2026-03-28T20:56:12Z - call_id=abc123 - tokens=120450
2026-03-28T20:58:03Z - call_id=abc124 - tokens=980000
2026-03-28T21:01:04Z - call_id=abc125 - tokens=50
```

ryan-ops: It looks like they used ~1.1M tokens in a short window. Hosted monthly credits were ~1.5M remaining at 00:00 UTC start-of-month? I still need to reconcile.

tim-billing: I checked billing events — there was a plan amendment on 2026-03-01 with proration that created a reduced remaining-window length for their prior cycle. That created a custom reset timestamp for the cycle which our x-credits-reset header reports. The combined effect with their heavy burst at 20:58 caused depletion before the standard 00:00 UTC refill.

maria-support: So cause looks like proration-created a non-standard reset timestamp plus their large burst. Customer is upset because they expected monthly refill at local midnight. How should we explain and what remediation do we offer?

jordan-cs: Action items: 1) Explain refill is 00:00 UTC by default except when proration or manual billing adjustments create a custom window. 2) Share their account-specific reset timestamp and the events that set it. 3) Offer a one-time emergency top-up or temporary quota increase while they adjust schedules. 4) Recommend burst mitigation: lower max tokens per job, enable automatic batching suggestions, or move heavy nightly job after their confirmed reset time.

tim-billing: I've prepared a short excerpt they can include with the explanation: 

"Per account metadata, your current monthly window has a custom reset at 2026-03-28T21:00:00Z due to a plan change/proration on 2026-03-01. This means your current quota window ended at 21:00 UTC on 2026-03-28 and subsequently refilled at the next reset, not at local midnight. Future cycles will follow the standard 00:00 UTC unless we apply a billing timezone migration. If you prefer monthly cycles aligned to Europe/Berlin local midnight, we can evaluate a timezone-aligned billing migration (enterprise-only change)."

maria-support: Customer just replied: "We never requested a plan change. Can you show the exact event?"

tim-billing: Here's the event log entry (sanitized): 

```
event_id: evt_51xJ
created_at: 2026-03-01T12:07:31Z
actor: billing-system (proration worker)
action: apply_plan_proration
notes: applied promotion credit and shortened previous cycle by 9 days
```

maria-support: Customer says they were unaware of a promotion. What language should I use to de-escalate?

jordan-cs: Be transparent, provide timestamps and the headers they captured, explain technical cause (proration shortened window + heavy burst), and offer concrete fix: immediate 200k token emergency grant + free rerun credit for missed nightly job OR rollback the proration if it was applied incorrectly. Ask if they want billing ticket to rollback.

ryan-ops: Also mention how they can prevent future surprises: 1) Monitor x-credits-remaining header on responses; 2) Use /v1/usage API to pull remaining credits programmatically and gate nightly jobs; 3) Set an alerts rule in Console for remaining credits < 10%.

maria-support: I've drafted the reply and offered the emergency grant plus a billing rollback option. Customer accepted the grant and asked for logs proving the proration. I attached the event snippet and our support reference number.

maria-support: Follow-up note for internal: We should add a quick guidance doc in support playbooks clarifying "proration-created resets" and how to read x-credits-reset vs. 00:00 UTC expectation. Also add a short snippet in Console UX where we surface "Account reset timestamp (UTC)" prominently on billing page to avoid this confusion.

auto-billing-bot: NOTE: emergency_grant applied to ACCT-998: grant_id=grant_802a amount=200000 tokens expires=2026-04-05T00:00:00Z

maria-support: Closing loop — customer confirmed nightly job succeeded after our grant and will reschedule heavy jobs to after our standard reset. Marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
